liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Fire On The Mountain** (3 reviews): Scarlet>Fire is excellent, with interesting clapping from Mickey; Fire on the Mountain is interesting [11][13][20]
- **Built To Last** (2 reviews): First set is strong except Built to Last; crowd is responsive; Built to Last is uneven in quality [19][22]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (2 reviews): Scarlet/Fire is really good, with some reggae-flavored jams; Scarlet>Fire is remembered as one of the best versions seen, bringing the house down [17][21]
- **Mississippi Half-Step Uptown Toodeloo** (1 review): Opening Mississippi Half-Step is tight and infectious [22]
- **Candyman** (1 review): Candyman features nice guitar licks and a standout delivery of a menacing line [19]
- **Touch Of Grey** (1 review): Strong Touch of Grey closes the first set [11]
- **Standing On The Moon** (1 review): Fans were especially pleased to hear the new songs, particularly Standing on the Moon [14]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (1 review): Lovelight is very different from typical versions [13]

## The recordings

- **gd1989-03-27.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.81528.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 19 songs; 151 min; rated 3.23/5 by 13 [1]
- **gd1989-03-27.147894.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 150 min [2]
- **gd1989-03-27.147800.sbd.ultramatrix.miller.flac24**: soundboard; 19 songs; 150 min [3]
- **gd1989-03-27.158251.MTX.photoLeon.t-flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 153 min [4]
- **gd89-03-27.schoeps.wiley.9204.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 19 songs; 152 min; rated 3.83/5 by 18 [5]. Said about its sound: Sound quality is not great, though some tracks are worth hearing; The audience recording captures the crowd clearly [17][21]

## Around the show

- Reviewer's first Dead show, attended on a free ticket from an acquaintance [11]
- Garcia bopped around the stage energetically, and the audience's enthusiasm is audible on the tape [14]
- Jerry sings one song forcefully with lots of energy, stressing certain words [18]
- Reviewer recalls Jerry being very animated that night [21]
- Opened the Spring '89 tour; the Omni's energy is palpable on the tape [22]
- Standing on the Moon is shorter than later versions because it initially lacked the closing jam [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1989-03-27.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.81528.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG90) D [1]. Also: Soundboard with Schoeps CMC4/MK4 audience-source patches to Mississippi Half Step, via DAT and CD; tapes from Paul Scotton and Joani Walker [1]
- **gd1989-03-27.147894.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: taped by Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering By Charlie Miller  October 24, 2019; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG90) [2]
- **gd1989-03-27.147800.sbd.ultramatrix.miller.flac24**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG90) [3]. Also: Soundboard recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy, transferred and mastered by Charlie Miller; Schoeps patches fill Mississippi Half Step gaps [3]
- **gd1989-03-27.158251.MTX.photoLeon.t-flac16**: source: Matrix created in Adobe Audition by Joe Noel August 04, 2022 [4]. Also: Matrix blending soundboard with Baker's audience tape and Tim Wiley's Schoeps recording; soundboard processed by Charlie Miller [4]
- **gd89-03-27.schoeps.wiley.9204.sbeok.shnf**: source: AUD(Schoeps CMC-441's)>DAT>CDR [5]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead The Omni - March 27, 1989](https://www.dead.net/show/march-27-1989) [24]
- Poster by D.King Gallery: [Grateful Dead 3/27/1989 Atlanta Backstage Pass](https://www.dking-gallery.com/store/Dead_Pass_890327.html) [25]
